name: MindrianOS Opportunity Discovery
purpose: Explore uncertainty, especially wicked challenges, for source-linked opportunity hypotheses across an authorized MindrianOS room or portfolio scope; help people investigate selected paths while preserving uncertainty, competing frames, and human qualification.

mindrianos: canonical room-local graph access through MindrianOS navigation and authorized bounded projections
user objective, scope, exclusions, and approvals
external research retrieval and grant validation
ICM run record, graph writes, opportunity portfolio, and truth/disposition transitions
mindrian_eureka: validation and execution of selected bounded capabilities
job lifecycle, engine/runtime provenance, and candidate output validation
source-linked discovery signals and proposed next-host-action metadata

rules: Never infer room authorization from a room name, scope_id, filesystem path, or research_grant_id.
Never run all capabilities by default; select methods for the user's objective and state why.
Explore uncertainty as potential opportunity terrain; do not force a wicked challenge into one problem frame or a single predicted future.
Never treat a retrieval score, pair, analogy, or generated claim as verified opportunity evidence.
Never let Eureka read room paths, fetch outside research, write MindrianOS graph state, or qualify a candidate.
A failed, blocked, partial, or empty run must remain distinguishable from a completed run with no useful candidates.
Preserve stable source IDs, source references, hashes, snapshot ID, method version, and uncertainty through every handoff.

theo_checkpoints.when: Before capability selection, when the task would benefit from framework or method guidance.
theo_checkpoints.send: A generic problem class or framework/concept lookup supported by Theo's current MCP contract; do not send room content unless the available Theo operation explicitly accepts it and room policy permits it.
theo_checkpoints.expect: Method, concept, or review guidance that helps frame the investigation.
theo_checkpoints.must_not_claim: Theo evaluated the room or validated a candidate.

theo_checkpoints.when: After a candidate has a source trail and before human qualification, if Theo exposes a case-capable review operation for this data boundary.
theo_checkpoints.send: Only the minimum authorized candidate context accepted by that operation, with source and confidentiality policy checked.
theo_checkpoints.expect: A bounded critique, evidence gaps, alternatives, or next discriminating question.
theo_checkpoints.must_not_claim: A generic review guide or framework lookup is a case-specific Theo review.

stages.action: Resolve the active room once; read /mos:status and inspect the user-selected material. Treat status as a summary, not a complete inventory.
stages.approval: Confirm scope only when room policy or ambiguity requires it.
stop_if: Required source data cannot be read

stages.action: Record objective, desired decision, constraints, exclusions, and evidence standard. Use Theo/framework guidance when it improves method selection. Read scout_capabilities and choose only suitable available capabilities.
stages.approval: Ask before materially changing the objective or expanding the data boundary.
stop_if: Essential objective or scope is unresolved
No suitable capability or prerequisite is unavailable

stages.action: Build the method-specific bounded projection from the already-authorized scope. For document-oriented methods, provide stable IDs, resolvable source refs, title, text, source hash, corpus label, and snapshot identity. For graph methods, read the room-local graph through MindrianOS navigation and provide stable node/edge IDs, selected authorized text/source fields, typed relations, snapshot identity, and explicit omissions. Do not pass room paths, credentials, unrestricted raw properties, or the visualization-only graph export.
stages.approval: Approval required if scope policy requires it or if content will cross the local boundary.

stages.action: For durable RS jobs, call scout_plan with the objective and exact authorized bundle. For synchronous supporting stages, inspect scout_capability and use scout_run_workflow or the typed HSI/Jason tool. Return readiness, prerequisites, model/runtime, network behavior, limits, and expected output. For the one-command run of both pair engines, call scout_plan_pair_screen and present its plan.
stages.approval: MindrianOS presents the plan and obtains any required run approval.

stages.action: Start approved RS jobs with scout_start or the local RS+HSI scout with scout_start_opportunity_signal_scout; MindrianOS retains job_id, polls scout_status, supports scout_cancel, then retrieves scout_result. Other current stages are synchronous and do not have durable job recovery yet. After the host approval, start it with scout_start_pair_screen, passing the plan digest and the approval reference.

When the approved pair scan returns candidates and MindrianOS has same-model vectors for the paired artifacts, room cohort, and framework baseline, optionally call portfolio.discover_hsi_whitespace with those inputs from the same snapshot. Carry the selected pair IDs and nearest artifact/framework IDs back into the room-bound investigation; interpret the density signal as a local lead only.
stop_if: HSI pair IDs cannot be resolved in the same snapshot

stages.action: When an HSI whitespace stage returns zones, optionally call portfolio.interpret_whitespace with those zones and an authorized projection of the same snapshot's ADDRESSES_PROBLEM_TYPE and FEEDS_INTO framework edges. For pair-seeded zones, map the leading supplied baseline framework ID/name into the framework fields expected by the interpreter. Preserve stable framework and artifact IDs. Let the returned classification and question inform Theo's next method choice; keep Wicked, Un-Defined, Ill-Defined, and Well-Defined paths distinct. The engine returns a three-part exploration prompt for Theo; it does not call a model or execute the suggested next action.
stop_if: Framework mapping is absent or stale
A requested framework ID cannot be resolved

stages.action: When the authorized HSI/RS analysis identifies a reverse salient with a known target section, optionally call portfolio.discover_rs_whitespace using source-linked target-section artifacts, same-model framework vectors, and the bottleneck source/target references from the same snapshot. Use the returned coverage and vocabulary signals as leads for what may lie downstream of the bottleneck; do not treat a low score as a validated opportunity.

Resolve source refs and present the candidate with its source excerpts and limitations. For selected pairs, run /mos:find-connections to trace room graph relationships and prior art. Do not run the command for every candidate when the shortlist is large; use a bounded, user-visible selection.

When outside evidence is needed, prepare exact questions with the selected research method, obtain host approval, retrieve evidence through MindrianOS's approved research service, and preserve source/claim lineage. Eureka may validate a returned bundle or map reviewed structures, but it does not fetch sources.
stages.approval: Required before any outbound query or transfer.

stages.action: For a candidate with a traceable evidence packet, present /mos:qualify-opportunity. The user accepts, rejects, parks, or requests more work.

Write only through the host's approved graph/portfolio path. Record the source snapshot, candidate lineage, engine/method versions, evidence, uncertainty, human disposition, and rejected/parked reason. Link or deduplicate across rooms without replacing the existing portfolio.

execution_surfaces.mindrianos_cli: The existing /mos:eureka workflow owns orchestration and native /mos command execution. It should use this capability MCP when configured. A direct engine CLI may be used as an explicit fallback only over the same prepared bundle and approval boundary.
execution_surfaces.mcp: The host invokes scout_capabilities, scout_plan/start/status/result/cancel for RS, scout_run_workflow for a selected supporting stage, typed HSI/Jason tools, and SME/OMM tools. MCP tools execute only Eureka-owned work and return data/metadata to the host. For the one-command run of both pair engines, the host calls scout_plan_pair_screen, shows the plan, obtains the approval, then calls scout_start_pair_screen with the plan digest and an approval reference, and uses the existing scout_status and scout_result tools.
execution_surfaces.direct_engine_cli: Descriptive engine CLIs such as eureka-pair-scout and eureka-signal-scout run a named method over an explicit input bundle; they are not substitutes for MindrianOS authorization and review. Legacy acronym aliases remain available.

catalog_scale_notes.unit: One catalog technology per artifact, with stable technology ID, source URL, title, category path, description, and source hash.
catalog_scale_notes.discovery_output: A bounded, source-linked shortlist of candidate pairs plus run coverage, warnings, and snapshot provenance.
catalog_scale_notes.downstream: MindrianOS chooses candidates for connection tracing, external evidence development, and human qualification; it does not treat the full pair ranking as a portfolio of validated opportunities.
